chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn al-Sindī and al-'Abbās, all of them, from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
That the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) resided in Medina for ten years and did not perform Hajj.
Then God revealed to him: 'And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep pass.'

He ordered the announcers to announce with their loudest voices that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) would perform Hajj from this year. Those present in Medina, the dependents, and the Bedouins learned of this and gathered. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) performed Hajj, and they were merely followers, waiting to see what command was given to them so they would do it, or what he did so they would do it.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) departed on the remaining four days of Dhu al-Qi'dah. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, the sun set, then he performed ghusl, then he went out until he reached the mosque near the tree, and prayed Dhuhr there. He intended Hajj as a standalone Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad).

He went out until he reached al-Bayda' at the first mile. The people formed two rows for him. He responded to the call with 'Hajj al-Mufrad' and brought the sacrificial animals, sixty-four or sixty-six, until he reached Mecca at the end of the four days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

He performed Tawaf around the House seven circuits and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Then he returned to the Stone and kissed it, having already kissed it at the beginning of his Tawaf.
Then he said: 'Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So begin with what God began with.'

And indeed, the Muslims used to think that the Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah was something invented by the polytheists. So God the Exalted revealed: 'Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs 'Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them.'
Then he went to al-Safa, climbed it, faced the Yemeni Corner, praised God and extolled Him, and supplicated for the duration of reciting Surah al-Baqarah, reciting slowly.
Then he descended to al-Marwah and stood upon it as he had stood upon al-Safa, until he finished his Sa'i.
Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him while he was on al-Marwah, and ordered him to order the people to perform Talbiyah (exit Ihram), except for the one bringing the sacrificial animal.
A man said: 'Should we exit Ihram before we have finished our rituals?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stood on al-Marwah after finishing the Sa'i, he turned his face to the people, praised God and extolled Him.'
Then he said: 'Indeed, this is Gabriel (peace be upon him), and he gestured with his hand behind him, ordering me to order those who did not bring a sacrificial animal to exit Ihram.'

And if I had received the command from the beginning as I received it from behind, I would have done what I ordered you to do. But I brought the sacrificial animal, and it is not fitting for the one bringing the sacrificial animal to exit Ihram until the sacrificial animal reaches its place.'
He said: 'A man from the people said to him: We will surely exit as pilgrims with our hair dripping (wet with oil or sweat).'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Indeed, you will never believe after this.'
Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Kinani said to him: 'O Messenger of God, we have been taught our religion as if we were created today.'
Is this which you ordered us to do for this year of ours, or for what comes after?
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'No, it is for eternity until the Day of Resurrection.'
Then he interlaced his fingers, some with others, and said: 'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection.'

Ali (peace be upon him) arrived from Yemen to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) while he was in Mecca. He entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her), and she had already exited Ihram.
He found a sweet scent and found her wearing dyed clothes. He said: 'What is this, O Fatimah?'
She said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered us to do this.'
Ali (peace be upon him) went out to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), seeking a ruling, inciting against Fatimah (peace be upon her).
He said: 'O Messenger of God, I saw Fatimah had exited Ihram and was wearing dyed clothes.'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I ordered the people to do that. And you, O Ali, with what did you enter Ihram?'
He said: 'I said: O Messenger of God, an Ihram like the Ihram of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Be upon your Ihram like me, and you are my partner in my sacrificial animal.'
He said: 'And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) descended in Mecca at al-Batha', he and his companions.
And he did not stay in the houses.
When it was the day of Tarwiyah, at the setting of the sun, he ordered the people to perform ghusl and enter Ihram for Hajj.
And this is the word of God which He revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'So follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif.'
So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his companions went out, entering Ihram for Hajj, until they reached Mina.
He prayed Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, the last 'Isha, and Fajr.
Then he departed in the morning, and the people with him. And Quraysh would depart from al-Muzdalifah, which is Jam'.
And they prevented the people from departing from it.
So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) came, and Quraysh hoped that his departure would be from where they used to depart.
So God revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Then depart from where the people have departed and ask God for forgiveness.'
Meaning Ibrahim, Isma'il, and Ishaq (peace be upon them) in their departure from it, and whoever came after them.
When Qurayah saw that the tent of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had passed, something entered their minds regarding what they had hoped for from departing from their place.
Until he reached Namirah, which is the valley of 'Unah, opposite the Arak trees. He pitched his tent, and the people pitched their tents near it.
When the sun set, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went out, and with him was his horse. He had performed ghusl and cut the Talbiyah.
Until he stood at the mosque. He exhorted the people, ordered them, and forbade them.
Then he prayed Dhuhr and 'Asr with one Adhan and two Iqamahs.
Then he proceeded to the standing place (Mawqif) and stood there.
So the people would rush to the fetlocks of his she-camel, standing beside her.
So he moved her away, and they did the same.
He said: 'O people, the place of the fetlocks of my she-camel is not the standing place (Mawqif), but all of this is the standing place.'
And he gestured with his hand to the standing place, so the people dispersed.
And he did the same at Muzdalifah.
He stood until the disk of the sun set.
Then he departed and ordered the people to proceed slowly.
Until he reached Muzdalifah, which is al-Mash'ar al-Haram. He prayed Maghrib and the last 'Isha with one Adhan and two Iqamahs.
Then he stayed until he prayed Fajr there.
And he hastened the weak ones of Banu Hashim during the night.
And he ordered them not to throw the Jamrah, the Jamrah of al-Aqabah, until the sun rises.
When the day illuminated for him, he departed until he reached Mina.
He threw the Jamrah of al-Aqabah.
And the sacrificial animal that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) brought was sixty-four or sixty-six.
And Ali (peace be upon him) brought thirty-four or thirty-six.
So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) slaughtered from it sixty-six, and Ali (peace be upon him) slaughtered thirty-four camels.
And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that from each camel of them, a shoulder (or piece) of meat be taken.
Then it was thrown into a pot and cooked.
So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ate from it, and Ali (peace be upon him) drank its broth.
And he did not give the butchers its skins, nor its flanks, nor its necklaces.
And he gave it in charity.
And he shaved his head, visited the House, and returned to Mina.
So he stayed there until it was the third day from the end of the days of Tashriq.
Then he threw the Jamars and departed.
Until he reached al-Abtah.
So 'A'ishah said to him: 'O Messenger of God, your wives return with Hajj and 'Umrah together, and I return with Hajj only.'
So he stayed at al-Abtah and sent with her 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr to al-Tan'im.
So she entered Ihram for 'Umrah.
Then she came and performed Tawaf around the House and prayed two rak'ahs near the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
And she performed Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah.
Then she came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
So he departed on that day, and did not enter the mosque, nor perform Tawaf around the House.
And he entered from the upper part of Mecca from the path of the Medinans, and exited from the lower part of Mecca from Dhi Tuwa.'

key_terms.اَلتَّرْوِيَة: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, named for the carrying of water
key_terms.اَلْجَمْرَة: The stone pillars used in the ritual of stoning during Hajj
key_terms.اَلْحَلَق: Shaving the head, a ritual concluding Ihram for men
key_terms.اَلْعُمْرَة فِي اَلْحَجّ: The concept that 'Umrah is incorporated into Hajj, a ruling established for this pilgrimage
key_terms.اَلْمَوْقِف: The place of standing for prayer and supplication, specifically at Arafat or Muzdalifah
key_terms.حَجُّ اَلْمُفْرَد: Standalone Hajj, where the pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj only without 'Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the detailed rituals and rulings of the Prophet's Farewell Pilgrimage as narrated in Shia sources?
ai.summary: This comprehensive narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet’s Farewell Pilgrimage, highlighting the theological shift from pre-Islamic idolatrous practices to pure monotheism, particularly through the purification of Sa'i and the establishment of the Hajj rituals. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s explicit instruction to Ali regarding shared sacrificial duties and the integration of 'Umrah into Hajj, serving as a foundational text for understanding the legal and spiritual precedents of the pilgrimage.
